# QC part 3 — the genomic features: is the genome attached to each well the right organism?

## 1. What could possibly overlap

`gq01_name_overlap.csv`

| quantity | n |
|---|---|
| corroborated_db entries | 185 |
| corroborated_db_min5 entries | 87 |
| wells in the plate mapping | 298 |
| wells whose genome has non-empty KO annotation | 292 |
| genome 16S records (multi-copy) | 587 |
| assemblies carrying a 16S record | 375 |
| **wells with a genome 16S after mapping** | **233** |
| **ideal overlap: corroborated_db ∩ genome 16S** | **116** |
| ideal overlap: corroborated_db_min5 ∩ genome 16S | 54 |
| corroborated_db labels **not** in the plate mapping | 42 |

Two ceilings worth internalising before reading anything else. Only **233 of 298** wells have a
genome 16S at all, and the corroborated_db↔genome comparison can involve at most **116** labels —
not 185. 42 corroborated_db entries are not in the plate mapping whatsoever.

## 2. The reference-vs-reference control: corroborated_db against the genomes

No experiment involved — two independent references for the same well labels. This is the
best case any comparison here can achieve.

![identity and rank](outputs/figures/gq_f1_genome_identity_and_rank.png)

`gq03_vs_genome_16S_summary.csv`

| query | shared labels | median identity | ≥0.99 | ≥0.97 | ≥0.95 | ≥0.90 | **top-1** | top-5 | **top-10** | median rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **corroborated_db(185)** | 116 | **0.996** | 62.9% | 88.8% | 91.4% | 92.2% | **26.7%** | 57.8% | **69.0%** | **4** |
| 20260630 pair consensus | 82 | 0.961 | 35.4% | 42.7% | 68.3% | 82.9% | 23.2% | 41.5% | 43.9% | 22 |
| 20260721 pair consensus | 51 | 0.824 | 2.0% | 7.8% | 21.6% | 37.3% | **0.0%** | 3.9% | 3.9% | 116 |

**The control result is the important one.** Two references that should agree perfectly reach a
median identity of 0.996 — but the correct genome ranks **first only 26.7% of the time**, and
sits at median rank **4 of 233**. Identity is excellent; ranking is not. That is 16S degeneracy
in the genome reference space, and it caps what any rank-based verification can show.

So: **~27% top-1 / 69% top-10 is the practical ceiling**, not a failure. 20260630 at 23.2% /
43.9% is somewhat below that ceiling but the same regime. 20260721 at 0% / 3.9% is categorically
different — it is not near any ceiling, it simply does not match.

> ⚠️ genome 16S is **multi-copy** — 587 records across 375 assemblies — and the best-matching
> copy per strain is taken. Correct for identification, but it flatters the reference: a strain
> with several divergent copies gets several chances. These numbers are an upper bound on
> genome_16S's reliability.

## 3. Worst-ranked strains

`gq04_worst_strains.csv` — labels whose own genome sits far down the list while some *other*
genome matches perfectly. Candidates for a wrong genome assignment or a bad 16S in the assembly.

**20260630** (worst 8 of 82):

| label | identity to own genome | rank | best match | its identity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G9 | 0.753 | 212/233 | O9 | 1.000 |
| M11 | 0.755 | 210 | O11 | 1.000 |
| H5 | 0.761 | 209 | O23 | 1.000 |
| O15 | 0.760 | 204 | P15 | 1.000 |
| O13 | 0.758 | 203 | O9 | 1.000 |
| F23 | 0.764 | 190 | O11 | 1.000 |
| J3 | 0.766 | 189 | O11 | 1.000 |
| E20 | 0.767 | 184 | O11 | 1.000 |

**corroborated_db itself** has the same failure mode (O12 rank 228, O15 rank 210, D1 rank 207),
which is the clearest evidence that these are *genome-side* problems: the same labels fail for a
reference built independently of both experiments. Note `O15` appears in both lists, and several
20260630 labels point at the same few genomes (`O11`, `O9`) — consistent with a handful of
assemblies carrying 16S that matches many things, rather than 8 independent mapping errors.

## 4. ML justification — the mapping is real for 20260630

Despite the modest 16S agreement, the mapping carries genuine predictive signal. Test: attach KO
features through the mapping, then compare against **5 permuted well→genome assignments**, which
preserve the genomes, labels and pair structure and destroy only the correspondence.

`genomic_ml_join_test/outputs/j02_verdicts_refix.csv`

| experiment | regime | R² true | R² permuted | z | beats all permutations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **20260630** | cv_pair | 0.670 | 0.392 ± 0.079 | **+3.52** | ✅ |
| **20260630** | **cv_strain** | **0.181** | −0.351 ± 0.129 | **+4.13** | ✅ |
| 20260721 | cv_pair | 0.441 | 0.443 ± 0.034 | −0.03 | ❌ |
| 20260721 | **cv_strain** | −0.210 | −0.305 ± 0.138 | +0.69 | ❌ |

**20260630's mapping beats a random one at z = +4.1 on held-out strains.** 20260721's sits
exactly on the permutation mean (z = −0.03). The same holds for the yield target
(`genomic_ml_yield/outputs/n02_verdict.csv`: 20260721 cv_strain z = −0.06).

Read `cv_strain`, not `cv_pair`: a consistently-*wrong* bijection still gives every well a unique
KO fingerprint, so a model that has seen a strain's other pairs can score well knowing no
biology. That is exactly how 20260721 posts R² = 0.441 under `cv_pair` while being meaningless.

## 5. ML caveat — dropping poorly-matching strains *improves* the model

`qc07_strain_tier_sensitivity.csv`

| target | strain set | strains | pairs | R² | ρ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| relative abundance | all | 74 | 1465 | 0.321 | 0.576 |
| relative abundance | **corroborated-confirmed** | 46 | 568 | **0.364** | **0.721** |
| yield | all | 88 | 3828 | 0.233 | 0.568 |
| yield | corroborated-confirmed | 46 | 1035 | −0.132 | 0.422 |

**For relative abundance, restricting to verified strains raises ρ from 0.576 to 0.721** — and
this is not a sample-size artifact, because that target's strain learning curve is flat past ~45
strains (`genomic_ml/outputs/g06_strain_curve.csv`: ρ 0.631 at 45, 0.596 at 74). The unverified
strains were adding noise. **Default the relative-abundance analysis to this subset.**

**For yield the same comparison is confounded** and must not be read as a verification effect:
yield's strain curve is steep (R² −0.357 at 45 strains, +0.265 at 88), so halving the strain
count is expected to hurt on its own.

The strictest tier — 17 strains confirmed by two independent references — is too small to fit at
all. "Confirmed twice" is not an achievable standard with this collection.

## Takeaways

1. **Ceilings first.** Only 233/298 wells have a genome 16S; corroborated_db↔genome can involve
   at most 116 labels; and even reference-vs-reference tops out at 27% top-1 / median rank 4.
2. **Identity and rank disagree, and rank is the honest one.** corroborated_db reaches 0.996
   median identity yet ranks the right genome first only 27% of the time.
3. **genome_16S should not be used as an identity reference** (see QC_01 §4b), but it is
   adequate as a *rough* corroborator when read against its own ceiling.
4. **20260630's mapping is real** (z = +4.1 vs permuted, held-out strains); **20260721's is not**
   (z = −0.03).
5. **Restricting to corroborated-confirmed strains improves relative abundance** and should be
   the default there; the equivalent claim for yield is untestable with current strain counts.
